questions.stem: India's first National Park, established in 1936, is now known as:

options.option_text: Kaziranga National Park
Jim Corbett National Park (originally 'Hailey National Park')
Sundarbans National Park
Kanha National Park

questions.explanation: Established as Hailey National Park in 1936 (Uttarakhand) by United Provinces Governor Sir Malcolm Hailey. Renamed in 1957 after legendary hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett. India's first National Park; also the launchpad of Project Tiger (1973). Located in Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts, ~520 km². Major fauna — Bengal tigers, Asian elephants, leopards, ghariyals in River Ramganga.

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park is famous for housing the world's largest population of:

options.option_text: Asiatic lions
Greater one-horned rhinoceros
Snow leopards
Indian wild ass

questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam, on Brahmaputra floodplain) — UNESCO WHS 1985, declared NP in 1974, Tiger Reserve 2007. Home to ~2,613 Indian one-horned rhinos (2022 census), ~70% of the global population. Other 'Big Five': Asian elephant, wild water buffalo, Bengal tiger, Eastern swamp deer (state animal of Assam). Annual flooding from Brahmaputra is a natural recharge for grasslands but also a threat to wildlife crossing NH-37 to higher ground.

questions.stem: The only National Park in the world located within a major city's metropolitan limits is:

options.option_text: Sanjay Gandhi NP, Mumbai
Sultanpur NP, Gurugram
Keoladeo NP, Bharatpur
Indira Gandhi NP, Delhi

questions.explanation: Sanjay Gandhi NP (formerly Borivali NP) — 104 km² inside Mumbai's Greater Bombay area. Around 35-40 leopards live within metropolitan limits — the highest density in any urban-adjacent landscape worldwide. Houses the 2,400-year-old Kanheri Buddhist caves. Other distinctions: Hemis NP (Ladakh) — India's largest by area (~4,400 km²); Mahatma Gandhi Marine NP (A&N) — first Marine NP. There is no 'Indira Gandhi NP' in Delhi (that name applies to Pollachi-Anaimalai TR in TN).

questions.stem: Match the National Park with its state — which pairing is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Bandhavgarh — Madhya Pradesh
Gir — Karnataka
Periyar — Kerala
Hemis — Ladakh

questions.explanation: Gir National Park is in GUJARAT — not Karnataka — Junagadh, Saurashtra region. Last home of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica), ~674 lions (2020 census). Bandhavgarh — MP, highest tiger density in India. Periyar — Kerala, around Periyar Lake, named after the river. Hemis — Ladakh, India's largest NP, snow leopard habitat. Karnataka's main NPs include Bandipur, Nagarahole, Bhadra, Anshi.

questions.stem: Sundarbans — a UNESCO World Heritage Site straddling India and Bangladesh — is most famous for:

options.option_text: Asiatic Cheetah
Royal Bengal Tigers and the world's largest mangrove forest
Snow Leopards
Hangul deer

questions.explanation: Sundarbans NP (West Bengal) — declared NP 1984, UNESCO WHS 1987. Contains the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest (~10,000 km² across India + Bangladesh). Home to 96 Bengal tigers (Indian portion, 2022 census) — these are unique 'salt-water tigers' that swim across creeks. Other species: estuarine crocodile, Gangetic dolphin, Olive Ridley turtles. Mangrove species — Heritiera fomes (sundari, the namesake), Avicennia, Rhizophora.

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in 1973. Its initial 9 tiger reserves did NOT include:

options.option_text: Corbett (Uttarakhand)
Bandipur (Karnataka)
Periyar (Kerala) — added later
Manas (Assam)

questions.explanation: Project Tiger inaugurated 1 April 1973, kicked off at Jim Corbett. Original 9 reserves: Corbett, Manas, Ranthambore, Palamau, Sariska, Kanha, Melghat, Bandipur, Sunderbans. Periyar added in 1978 (10th). India now has 58 Tiger Reserves (Mar 2025) covering ~75,000 km². Tiger count: 3,167 (2022 census, +6.7% over 2018). Ranthambore is famous for its 'royal cubs' visible from open jeeps; Bandipur for forest fires of 2019.

questions.stem: India's largest National Park by area is:

options.option_text: Jim Corbett, Uttarakhand
Hemis, Ladakh
Kaziranga, Assam
Sundarbans, West Bengal

questions.explanation: Hemis NP — ~4,400 km² in eastern Ladakh. Home to ~200 snow leopards (highest density anywhere). Established 1981 to protect endangered Himalayan fauna — bharal (blue sheep), Tibetan wolf, Eurasian lynx, ibex. The Hemis monastery (1672) is within the park. India's smallest NP — South Button Island (Andaman & Nicobar) at 0.03 km².

questions.stem: Gir Forest National Park in Gujarat is the world's sole natural habitat of which large cat species?

options.option_text: Snow Leopard (Panthera uncia), found mainly in the Himalayas
Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica), a critically endangered subspecies
Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris), widespread across central India
Indian Leopard (Panthera pardus fusca), found in most Indian forests

questions.explanation: Gir Forest NP in Saurashtra is the last surviving natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica). The Bengal Tiger ranges across central and northeastern India, not Gir. Snow Leopard is restricted to Himalayan high-altitude zones. Indian Leopard is widespread — none is exclusive to Gir the way the Asiatic Lion is.

questions.stem: Manas National Park, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985 and a Project Tiger reserve, is located in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Meghalaya, bordering the Garo Hills region near Bangladesh
Nagaland, situated along the border with Myanmar (Burma)
Assam, in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayan range
Arunachal Pradesh, spread across the trans-Himalayan river valleys

questions.explanation: Manas NP lies in Assam on the Indo-Bhutan border and is a UNESCO WHS (1985), Project Tiger reserve, and Biosphere Reserve. Arunachal Pradesh is a common distractor because Namdapha NP is there; Meghalaya has Nokrek Biosphere Reserve — neither is Manas.

questions.stem: Eravikulam National Park in Kerala was established primarily to protect which Schedule-I endangered ungulate?

options.option_text: Sambar deer (Rusa unicolor), the largest deer species found in India
Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius), an endangered mountain goat
Gaur (Bos gaurus), the largest wild bovine animal in peninsular India
Malabar large-spotted civet, a critically endangered nocturnal carnivore

questions.explanation: Eravikulam NP in the Munnar hills of Kerala holds the world's largest viable population of the Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius), which is endemic to the Western Ghats. Gaur and Sambar occur widely across multiple parks; the Malabar civet is found in lowland Kerala, not at the high-altitude Eravikulam grasslands.

questions.stem: Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh is unique for sheltering all four large felid species. Which combination correctly identifies them?

options.option_text: Tiger, Asiatic Lion, Leopard, and Snow Leopard
Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard
Tiger, Cheetah, Leopard, and Clouded Leopard
Tiger, Jaguar, Leopard, and Snow Leopard

questions.explanation: Namdapha hosts the Bengal Tiger, Common Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard — making it one of very few areas globally with four big-cat species. Option A is wrong because the Asiatic Lion is restricted to Gir (Gujarat), not Arunachal Pradesh. Cheetah is functionally extinct in India; Jaguar is a New World species.

questions.stem: The Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP), inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014, lies within which district of Himachal Pradesh?

options.option_text: Lahaul-Spiti, the cold desert plateau north of the Rohtang Pass
Chamba, bordering the Ravi river catchment near Jammu region
Kullu, within the Beas and Tirthan river catchment area
Kinnaur, along the Sutlej river valley bordering Tibet (China)

questions.explanation: GHNP (1,171 sq km) lies in Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh and was declared a UNESCO WHS in 2014 for its exceptional temperate and alpine biodiversity. Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur are cold-desert trans-Himalayan districts; Chamba has the Khajjiar meadow but not GHNP. Tirthan Valley, part of GHNP's buffer zone, confirms the Kullu location.

questions.stem: Pench Tiger Reserve, widely linked to the landscape of Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book', straddles the territorial boundary of which two Indian states?

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (Balaghat and Rajnandgaon districts)
Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh (Nagpur and Rajnandgaon districts)
Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Kota and Sheopur district boundary)
Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra (Seoni–Chhindwara and Nagpur districts)

questions.explanation: Pench straddles Seoni and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh and Nagpur district of Maharashtra. Kipling's 'Seonee Hills' reference the Seoni (MP) side. Option A is the most common error — Balaghat (MP) borders Rajnandgaon (CG), but that is Indravati corridor territory, not Pench.

questions.stem: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park in upper Assam is most distinctively known for which rare wildlife population not commonly found elsewhere in India's protected areas?

options.option_text: Wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) in a protected river-island refuge
Gangetic river dolphin (Platanista gangetica) in an enclosed river stretch
Feral horses (semi-wild Equus caballus) surviving in open floodplain grasslands
Golden langur (Trachypithecus geei) isolated to a single riparian forest

questions.explanation: Dibru-Saikhowa NP is uniquely famous for its population of feral horses — descendants of animals used during World War II that escaped and reverted to semi-wild behaviour in the Lohit-Brahmaputra floodplains. Wild water buffalo exists in Manas and Kaziranga; Golden langur is associated with Chakrashila and Manas; Gangetic dolphin is found in river sanctuaries like Vikramshila — none is the defining feature of Dibru-Saikhowa.
